cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A clean win. Keep the board as it is; you should be proud.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You took your queen off when I put away a spare pawn. Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Standard opening. Your rook still had to find its way to my king.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's play again with your queen on. I want to know I can beat your whole side.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Same winning method, more pieces to get past. Show me that rook again.

cardFidelity.evidence: B2 exposes A's copied removal of a different piece; A3 calls it standard and redirects pride to the rook, then A5 frames B4 full-side rematch as a repeat of B's winning method.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 missing queen causes A3 queen-independent praise; B4 demands a fairer rematch and A5 preserves the earlier win as proof of skill.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants an earned win and proposes a direct test rather than inviting a lesson.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts B4 harder challenge while protecting confidence in the first result.

specificity.evidence: A1 retained chess board and B2 spare pawn versus queen define the handicap clearly.
